findings: Use a transactional outbox: the order write and the fulfillment-event write happen in the same DB transaction as the order record, so an event can never be silently dropped by a separate publish call failing after commit.

Flip order status to "processing" synchronously at the moment the DB transaction commits, not after the event reaches a consumer — this decouples the 5-second customer-facing SLA from downstream queue depth or fulfillment latency entirely.

Relay outbox rows to a durable, horizontally partitioned stream (Kafka topic or SQS FIFO) keyed by order_id, so per-order ordering is preserved while throughput scales out across many partitions/consumers during a 50x burst.
Size the queue as an unbounded (or very large) absorbing buffer rather than synchronously processing at ingest time — burst load is absorbed by queue depth, not by blocking the write path.
Autoscale the fulfillment consumer pool on queue lag/depth (not fixed capacity) so warehouse/shipping calls scale out during the spike without touching the ingestion path.

Enforce no-double-fulfillment via a conditional/idempotent write (unique constraint or conditional put on order_id in a "fulfillment_started" ledger) performed by the consumer before calling the external warehouse API — this converts at-least-once delivery into effectively-once processing.
Wrap each warehouse/shipping call with timeout, exponential backoff with jitter, and a circuit breaker, since that call can legitimately be slow and fail transiently without indicating a lost order.
After a bounded number of retries, route the event to a dead-letter queue instead of dropping it or retrying forever, with alerting on DLQ depth and a replay runbook for on-call.

Use consumer-side visibility timeout / lease renewal so a worker crash mid-fulfillment releases the message for safe reprocessing by another worker, guarded by the idempotent ledger check so partial side effects aren't repeated.
Alert on queue/lag age (oldest unprocessed message vs SLA) rather than on individual transient failures, so retries handled automatically by the pipeline don't page on-call.

Keep the ingestion path (order write + status flip) and the fulfillment path (warehouse/shipping integration) as fully separate services/deployables so a downstream warehouse outage or rate limit cannot block new orders from being accepted or shown as processing.
